cases.question: Using only the basic Section 23-22 table and the Section 12-10 FAR definition, does 42,000 square feet of residential floor area on a 10,000-square-foot R7A zoning lot containing standard residences fit the basic maximum, and what broader compliance conclusion remains outside those facts?

A 10,000-square-foot R7A zoning lot is proposed with 48,000 square feet of residential floor area and is merely described as containing qualifying affordable housing. What does the Section 23-22 table establish numerically, and what qualification and affordable-floor-area facts are still needed before concluding that the higher FAR is available?
Can a standard residential building in an R7A district be 90 feet tall under the basic height-and-setback table?
An R7A interior zoning lot contains 10,000 square feet. Can a standard residential development cover 8,500 square feet of the lot under the basic lot-coverage regulation?
An attached residential building is proposed on a 35-foot-wide interior zoning lot with a 20-foot rear yard. Is that sufficient under the standard rear-yard rule?
A through lot is 150 feet deep and the proposal provides a 20-foot rear yard equivalent. Is that enough when the lot's historical shallow-lot condition is unknown?

cases.question: Two separate apartment buildings containing more than three dwelling units each are proposed on the same zoning lot, do not connect at any level, are below 125 feet, and are 30 feet apart. Is the spacing sufficient?
A 1,500-square-foot architectural office is proposed in a C3 district. Is the professional office use permitted as-of-right under the underlying C3 use regulations?
A C4-4 zoning lot is proposed with retail on the ground floor and apartments above. Is the residential use permitted under the underlying use regulations?

An 80-unit R7A residential development is within the Inner Transit Zone; every unit's temporary certificate of occupancy, or final certificate if no temporary certificate is issued, will be issued after December 5, 2024, and no application qualifies for the pre-December 5, 2024 continuation in Section 11-333. How many accessory off-street residential parking spaces does Section 25-211 require for those units?

A zoning lot assembled in 2026 straddles two zoning districts, with more than 50 percent of its area in the less restrictive district. Can that majority district's use regulations automatically apply to the entire zoning lot under Section 77-11?

Two tax lots on the same block have the same owner but touch for only eight linear feet and were not historically one zoning lot. Can they now be treated as one zoning lot merely because they share ownership?

A 5,000-square-foot below-grade storage level has more than one-half of its floor-to-ceiling height below the applicable base plane and is not used for dwelling purposes. Does it count as zoning floor area?

A building contains a lawful non-conforming use, but active operation of substantially all of that use stopped for 30 continuous months even though the owner always intended to reopen it. Can the owner simply restart the use?

My 8,000-square-foot R6A lot is outside an MIH area. I want 31,000 square feet of residential floor area, including 6,200 square feet that I intend to make affordable. Since 31,000 square feet is below the R6A 3.90 FAR limit, can I build it?

We have a 200-foot-deep through lot in an R7A district. The design has residential wings facing both streets with a 30-foot-wide open area between them. Both wings rise to 100 feet. Is the 30-foot open area enough for the rear yard equivalent? The building and zoning lot contain no community-facility use.

We are planning a new 60-unit market-rate apartment building in an R6 district. It will be completed after December 5, 2024. The broker says it is close to a subway, so no parking should be required. Is that correct?

We have a 10,000-square-foot zoning lot in a verified M1-4/R7A Special Mixed Use District. We want 45,000 square feet of qualifying affordable residential floor area and 10,000 square feet of a fabrication use that has already been confirmed as permitted. Since R7A allows 5.01 FAR and M1-4 allows 2.00 FAR, can we combine them for 7.01 FAR?

A lawful 20,000-square-foot warehouse has operated continuously in an R6B district since 1980. It occupied the same 20,000 square feet on December 17, 1987, and has never been enlarged. We want to add 5,000 square feet. Aren’t nonconforming uses allowed a 25 percent enlargement?

Our 20,000-square-foot zoning lot is split by a district boundary: 8,000 square feet is in R7A and 12,000 square feet is in R8A. We want 110,000 square feet of standard market-rate residential floor area and plan to put most of the building on the R8A side. Can we use the R8A FAR for the whole lot?

We have a lawful 90,000-square-foot office building constructed in 1985 on a 15,000-square-foot C6-2 zoning lot. The lot is on a narrow street and entirely beyond 100 feet of a wide street. It is outside a special district and outside a special density area. We want to convert the entire building to 100 market-rate apartments without enlarging it. Is 100 units allowed, and how much recreation space is required?

We filed a new-building application for one building on November 20, 2024, and DOB issued the permit on December 4, 2024. By December 5, 2024, about 60 percent of the foundation work was complete. The design complies with the zoning rules that existed before City of Yes but not with the new rules. Can we keep building under the old zoning?

The property is confirmed to be in an MIH area that the owner says was established in 2017. We want one development with eight apartments and 10,000 square feet of residential floor area. The current tax lots were combined in 2025. Since the project has no more than 10 units and no more than 12,500 square feet, does it qualify for the MIH small-development exception?
